paragraphs.title: The Command to Camp by the Sea

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak at the beginning of the passage?
answers: Moses
Pharaoh
The Israelites
easy.explanation: The first verse says that the Lord spoke to Moses.

easy.question: Where were the Israelites commanded to camp?
answers: Inside Egypt
Before Pihahiroth, between Migdol and the sea
At Mount Sinai
easy.explanation: Verse 2 commands Moses to have the Israelites camp before Pihahiroth, between Migdol and the sea.

easy.question: Who would pursue the Israelites?
answers: Moses
The Israelites
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: Verse 4 says that Pharaoh would pursue the Israelites.

medium.question: Why would Pharaoh think that the Israelites were in trouble?
answers: The wilderness had shut them in, making them seem trapped
They had willingly returned to Egypt
They had asked Pharaoh for help
medium.explanation: Pharaoh would say that they were entangled in the land because the wilderness had shut them in.

medium.question: In the phrase “They are entangled in the land,” what does “entangled” mean?
answers: Happy and successful
Confused or trapped
Strong and organized
medium.explanation: The context shows that “entangled” means confused or trapped because the wilderness surrounded them.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in these verses?
answers: Pharaoh pursues them, then Israel camps, and finally Moses receives the command
Israel returns to Egypt, and then Pharaoh releases them
The Lord commands Israel where to camp, Pharaoh thinks they are trapped, and then he pursues them
medium.explanation: First the Lord gives the camping command, then Pharaoh concludes that Israel is trapped, and finally he pursues them.

challenge.question: Why does the Lord command the Israelites to camp in a place that seems closed in between the wilderness and the sea?
answers: To make Pharaoh think they are trapped and pursue them
To keep them permanently away from the sea
To hide them from Moses
challenge.explanation: Their location makes Pharaoh think that they have no way to escape, so he pursues them.

challenge.question: According to verse 4, what is the divine purpose of Pharaoh’s pursuit?
answers: To return the Israelites to slavery without any change
To gain honor through Pharaoh and his army and make the Egyptians know that the Lord is God
To punish Moses for bringing the people out
challenge.explanation: The Lord says that He will be honored through Pharaoh and his army, so that the Egyptians will know that He is the Lord.

challenge.question: What detail in verse 2 emphasizes that the Israelites camped facing the sea rather than at a general location nearby?
answers: They camped “before” Baalzephon, beside the sea
They camped inside Egypt
They camped beside a high mountain
challenge.explanation: The verse specifies that they camped before Baalzephon, beside the sea.

questions.question: Why does the Lord command the Israelites to camp in a place that seems closed in between the wilderness and the sea?
answers: To make Pharaoh think they are trapped and pursue them
To keep them permanently away from the sea
To hide them from Moses
questions.explanation: Their location makes Pharaoh think that they have no way to escape, so he pursues them.

questions.question: According to verse 4, what is the divine purpose of Pharaoh’s pursuit?
answers: To return the Israelites to slavery without any change
To gain honor through Pharaoh and his army and make the Egyptians know that the Lord is God
To punish Moses for bringing the people out
questions.explanation: The Lord says that He will be honored through Pharaoh and his army, so that the Egyptians will know that He is the Lord.

questions.question: What detail in verse 2 emphasizes that the Israelites camped facing the sea rather than at a general location nearby?
answers: They camped “before” Baalzephon, beside the sea
They camped inside Egypt
They camped beside a high mountain
questions.explanation: The verse specifies that they camped before Baalzephon, beside the sea.

easy.question: What caused Pharaoh and his servants to regret releasing Israel?
answers: They heard that the people had fled
They lost their possessions
They were afraid of the sea
easy.explanation: When they were told that Israel had fled, they regretted releasing them from slavery.

easy.question: Whom did Pharaoh take with him when he went after Israel?
answers: Only his servants
His people
Only his horsemen
easy.explanation: The passage says that Pharaoh took his people with him.

easy.question: What were the Israelites doing while Pharaoh pursued them?
answers: Returning to Egypt
Hiding in the wilderness
Going out boldly
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Israelites went out with a high hand, meaning boldly and confidently.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: Pharaoh pursued them, and afterward heard that Israel had fled
Israel fled, Pharaoh regretted releasing them, and then he pursued them
Israel reached the sea, and then Pharaoh released them
medium.explanation: First Pharaoh learned that Israel had fled; then he regretted it and went after them with his army.

medium.question: What does the phrase “went out with a high hand” mean?
answers: They went out boldly and confidently
They went out empty-handed
They went out quietly and secretly
medium.explanation: The context presents Israel leaving Egypt despite Pharaoh’s pursuit, so the phrase means boldly and confidently.

medium.question: Why did Pharaoh take many chariots and an army?
answers: To protect Egypt from a new enemy
To find a place to camp near the sea
To pursue and overtake the Israelites
medium.explanation: Pharaoh gathered his chariots, people, and soldiers because he intended to pursue and overtake Israel.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the mention of Pharaoh’s chariots, horsemen, and army?
answers: Pharaoh launched a large, organized military pursuit
Only Pharaoh took part in the pursuit
The Egyptians began a trading expedition
challenge.explanation: The details about the chariots, horsemen, and army show that this was a large military force, not a personal journey.

challenge.question: What striking contrast appears between Pharaoh and the Israelites in verse 8?
answers: Pharaoh came out of the sea while Israel entered Egypt
Pharaoh pursued, while Israel went out boldly
Pharaoh went out boldly, while Israel surrendered
challenge.explanation: The verse presents Pharaoh as pursuing Israel, while Israel leaves with confidence and strength.

challenge.question: What does “they overtook them encamping by the sea” tell us about the Israelites’ situation?
answers: They had already defeated the Egyptians
They were camped by the sea and had been reached by the Egyptian force
They had sailed away before the Egyptians arrived
challenge.explanation: The phrase says that Israel was camped beside the sea when the Egyptians caught up with them.

questions.question: What can we infer from the mention of Pharaoh’s chariots, horsemen, and army?
answers: Pharaoh launched a large, organized military pursuit
Only Pharaoh took part in the pursuit
The Egyptians began a trading expedition
questions.explanation: The details about the chariots, horsemen, and army show that this was a large military force, not a personal journey.

questions.question: What striking contrast appears between Pharaoh and the Israelites in verse 8?
answers: Pharaoh came out of the sea while Israel entered Egypt
Pharaoh pursued, while Israel went out boldly
Pharaoh went out boldly, while Israel surrendered
questions.explanation: The verse presents Pharaoh as pursuing Israel, while Israel leaves with confidence and strength.

questions.question: What does “they overtook them encamping by the sea” tell us about the Israelites’ situation?
answers: They had already defeated the Egyptians
They were camped by the sea and had been reached by the Egyptian force
They had sailed away before the Egyptians arrived
questions.explanation: The phrase says that Israel was camped beside the sea when the Egyptians caught up with them.

paragraphs.title: Israel Is Afraid, and Moses Encourages Them

easy.question: Whom did the Israelites see marching after them?
answers: The Egyptians
The Midianites
The Philistines
easy.explanation: The Israelites looked up and saw the Egyptians marching after them.

easy.question: How did the Israelites react when they saw the Egyptians?
answers: They rejoiced
They were very afraid and cried out to the Lord
They immediately returned to Egypt
easy.explanation: The passage says that they were greatly afraid and cried out to the Lord.

easy.question: What did Moses tell the Israelites to do?
answers: Flee into the wilderness
Fight the Egyptians
Do not be afraid, stand still, and see the Lord’s salvation
easy.explanation: Moses told them not to fear, but to stand still and see the Lord’s salvation.

medium.question: Why did the Israelites complain to Moses?
answers: They feared that the Egyptians would kill them in the wilderness
They did not want to receive food
They wanted to return to Egypt to celebrate
medium.explanation: When they saw the Egyptians approaching, they feared that they would die in the wilderness and complained.

medium.question: In “you shall hold your peace,” what does the phrase mean?
answers: You shall shout loudly
You shall be silent and refrain from acting
You shall hurry to fight
medium.explanation: Moses says that the Lord will fight for them, so they should remain quiet rather than act out of fear.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Moses fights, the people return to Egypt, and the Egyptians retreat
The people cross the sea, the Egyptians arrive, and Moses complains
The Egyptians approach, the people become afraid and complain, and Moses reassures them
medium.explanation: First the Egyptians approach; the people then become afraid and complain, and Moses strengthens and reassures them.

challenge.question: What does Moses promise in the words “you shall see them again no more for ever”?
answers: The Egyptians will no longer threaten them
The people will soon return to Egypt
The people will have to fight the Egyptians every day
challenge.explanation: Moses promises that this threatening encounter with the Egyptians will end and that they will never see them again.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between the Israelites’ response and Moses’ response?
answers: The Israelites wanted to fight, while Moses wanted to flee
The Israelites were afraid and wanted to return to Egypt, while Moses trusted in the Lord’s salvation
The Israelites rejoiced, while Moses complained
challenge.explanation: The Israelites focused on the danger and possible death, while Moses urged them to trust that the Lord would save them.

challenge.question: What can we infer from “The Lord shall fight for you; and you shall hold your peace”?
answers: The people must fight alone
The Lord will not intervene
The Lord will act to save the people, and they must remain calm and wait
challenge.explanation: The sentence assigns the roles: the Lord will fight for them, while the people should not act out of fear but wait quietly.

questions.question: What does Moses promise in the words “you shall see them again no more for ever”?
answers: The Egyptians will no longer threaten them
The people will soon return to Egypt
The people will have to fight the Egyptians every day
questions.explanation: Moses promises that this threatening encounter with the Egyptians will end and that they will never see them again.

questions.question: What is the main difference between the Israelites’ response and Moses’ response?
answers: The Israelites wanted to fight, while Moses wanted to flee
The Israelites were afraid and wanted to return to Egypt, while Moses trusted in the Lord’s salvation
The Israelites rejoiced, while Moses complained
questions.explanation: The Israelites focused on the danger and possible death, while Moses urged them to trust that the Lord would save them.

questions.question: What can we infer from “The Lord shall fight for you; and you shall hold your peace”?
answers: The people must fight alone
The Lord will not intervene
The Lord will act to save the people, and they must remain calm and wait
questions.explanation: The sentence assigns the roles: the Lord will fight for them, while the people should not act out of fear but wait quietly.

paragraphs.title: The Command to Move Forward and Divide the Sea

easy.question: What did the Lord command the Israelites to do?
answers: Speak and move forward
Return to Egypt
Stay where they were
easy.explanation: The Lord told Moses to command the Israelites to go forward.

easy.question: What did the Lord command Moses to do with his rod?
answers: Throw it into the sea
Lift it up and stretch out his hand over the sea
Give it to Pharaoh
easy.explanation: Moses was commanded to lift up his rod, stretch out his hand over the sea, and divide it.

easy.question: Who would come after the Israelites?
answers: The peoples of Canaan
Wilderness shepherds
The Egyptians, with Pharaoh, chariots, and horsemen
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Egyptians would follow Israel, including Pharaoh, his army, chariots, and horsemen.

medium.question: Why were the Israelites told to “go forward” after the Lord told Moses to speak to them?
answers: So they would advance rather than remain in danger
So they would return to Egypt
So they could wait for the Egyptians to arrive
medium.explanation: The command teaches the Israelites to move forward in faith instead of remaining between the sea and the Egyptians.

medium.question: In “I will get me honour upon Pharaoh,” what does the phrase mean?
answers: I will hide from Pharaoh
I will show my power and receive honor through what happens to Pharaoh
I will join Pharaoh’s army
medium.explanation: The Lord would display His greatness and power through what would happen to Pharaoh and his army.

medium.question: What order of events is presented in these verses?
answers: The Egyptians recognize the Lord, then Israel travels, and finally the sea is divided
Israel returns to Egypt, and Moses throws the rod into the sea
Israel moves forward, Moses divides the sea, and the Egyptians follow
medium.explanation: First Israel is told to move forward; then the sea is divided and they cross on dry ground, while the Egyptians follow.

challenge.question: Why does the Lord harden the hearts of the Egyptians and allow them to follow Israel?
answers: So the Egyptians will reach a situation in which the Lord’s power will be revealed to them
So the Egyptians can help Israel cross
So the Israelites will become slaves in Egypt again
challenge.explanation: The purpose is for the Lord to gain honor through Pharaoh and his army, so that the Egyptians will know that He is the Lord.

challenge.question: What is the difference between Moses’ role and the Lord’s action in these verses?
answers: Moses hardens the Egyptians’ hearts, while the Lord only watches
Moses acts through the rod and his hand, while the Lord hardens the Egyptians’ hearts and reveals His glory
Moses brings the Egyptians, while the Lord commands them to pursue
challenge.explanation: Moses is told to lift the rod and stretch out his hand, while the Lord hardens the Egyptians’ hearts and declares that He will be honored through them.

challenge.question: What does the repeated phrase “upon Pharaoh, upon his chariots, and upon his horsemen” emphasize?
answers: Only Pharaoh is involved
The chariots and horsemen are not part of Egypt’s army
The honor and divine revelation will be seen throughout Egypt’s military forces
challenge.explanation: The details show that not only Pharaoh but also his army and military equipment will be part of the event revealing the Lord’s power.

questions.question: Why does the Lord harden the hearts of the Egyptians and allow them to follow Israel?
answers: So the Egyptians will reach a situation in which the Lord’s power will be revealed to them
So the Egyptians can help Israel cross
So the Israelites will become slaves in Egypt again
questions.explanation: The purpose is for the Lord to gain honor through Pharaoh and his army, so that the Egyptians will know that He is the Lord.

questions.question: What is the difference between Moses’ role and the Lord’s action in these verses?
answers: Moses hardens the Egyptians’ hearts, while the Lord only watches
Moses acts through the rod and his hand, while the Lord hardens the Egyptians’ hearts and reveals His glory
Moses brings the Egyptians, while the Lord commands them to pursue
questions.explanation: Moses is told to lift the rod and stretch out his hand, while the Lord hardens the Egyptians’ hearts and declares that He will be honored through them.

questions.question: What does the repeated phrase “upon Pharaoh, upon his chariots, and upon his horsemen” emphasize?
answers: Only Pharaoh is involved
The chariots and horsemen are not part of Egypt’s army
The honor and divine revelation will be seen throughout Egypt’s military forces
questions.explanation: The details show that not only Pharaoh but also his army and military equipment will be part of the event revealing the Lord’s power.

paragraphs.title: The Pillar of Cloud Protects Israel

easy.question: Who moved from in front of Israel’s camp to behind it?
answers: The angel of God
The Egyptian camp
Moses
easy.explanation: The passage says that the angel of God, who had gone before Israel, moved behind them.

easy.question: What did the pillar of cloud do?
answers: It disappeared from the camp
It moved from in front of Israel to behind them
It went in front of the Egyptian camp
easy.explanation: The pillar of cloud moved from before the Israelites and stood behind them.

easy.question: Between whom did the cloud come?
answers: Between Moses and Aaron
Between the sea and the wilderness
Between the Egyptian camp and the Israelite camp
easy.explanation: The passage says that the cloud came between the two camps.

medium.question: What was the result of the cloud standing between the two camps?
answers: The Egyptians and Israelites did not come near each other all night
The Israelites returned to Egypt
The cloud disappeared immediately
medium.explanation: The cloud separated the camps, so one did not come near the other all night.

medium.question: In the phrase “it gave light by night,” what did the cloud do?
answers: It made the night darker
It provided light during the night
It moved the camps farther apart
medium.explanation: The verse says that the cloud gave light to the Israelites by night.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: The cloud gave light, then the angel moved, and finally the camps formed
The Egyptians moved away, then the cloud disappeared, and finally the angel arrived
The angel moved behind Israel, the cloud moved behind them, and then it came between the camps
medium.explanation: First the angel moved behind Israel, then the pillar of cloud moved there, and finally it stood between the camps.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the words “the one came not near the other all the night”?
answers: The separation between the camps lasted throughout the night
The camps met only in the morning
The Israelites marched all night
challenge.explanation: The words “all the night” emphasize that the camps remained separated throughout the night.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the cloud standing between the two camps?
answers: The cloud signaled Israel to return to Egypt
The cloud acted as a barrier separating Israel from Egypt
The cloud led the Egyptians through the wilderness
challenge.explanation: Its position between the camps, together with their lack of contact, shows that it created separation and protection.

challenge.question: What wording shows that it was the same angel who changed position?
answers: The verse mentions two camps
The verse mentions both cloud and darkness
It first says that the angel went before Israel and then that it moved behind them
challenge.explanation: The same angel is first described as going before Israel and then as moving behind them, showing that it changed position.

questions.question: What can we infer from the words “the one came not near the other all the night”?
answers: The separation between the camps lasted throughout the night
The camps met only in the morning
The Israelites marched all night
questions.explanation: The words “all the night” emphasize that the camps remained separated throughout the night.

questions.question: What can we understand from the cloud standing between the two camps?
answers: The cloud signaled Israel to return to Egypt
The cloud acted as a barrier separating Israel from Egypt
The cloud led the Egyptians through the wilderness
questions.explanation: Its position between the camps, together with their lack of contact, shows that it created separation and protection.

questions.question: What wording shows that it was the same angel who changed position?
answers: The verse mentions two camps
The verse mentions both cloud and darkness
It first says that the angel went before Israel and then that it moved behind them
questions.explanation: The same angel is first described as going before Israel and then as moving behind them, showing that it changed position.

easy.question: Who stretched out his hand over the sea?
answers: Moses
Pharaoh
Aaron
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Moses stretched out his hand over the sea.”

easy.question: What did the Lord do to the sea?
answers: He changed it into a river
He made it dry land
He sent it back to Egypt
easy.explanation: The Lord made the sea dry land, drying the sea floor.

easy.question: Where did the Israelites travel?
answers: Over a high mountain
Through the forest
Through the sea on dry ground
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Israelites went into the midst of the sea upon dry ground.

medium.question: What caused the sea to become dry?
answers: A strong east wind that blew all night
The sun heating the water
The Israelites drawing out the water
medium.explanation: The Lord drove back the sea with a strong east wind throughout the night, making it dry.

medium.question: In “the Lord made the sea dry land,” what happened to the sea?
answers: It became dry
It became deep
It became stormy
medium.explanation: The verse says that the sea became dry land so that Israel could cross.

medium.question: What happened after the waters were divided?
answers: The Israelites entered the sea on dry ground
Pharaoh built a wall
Moses returned to Egypt
medium.explanation: After the waters were divided, the Israelites crossed through the sea on dry ground.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the description “the waters were a wall”?
answers: The waters stood on both sides of the Israelites
The waters receded on only one side
The waters disappeared completely
challenge.explanation: The waters stood like walls beside the path, on the Israelites’ right and left; they did not disappear.

challenge.question: What does “all that night” show about the process described?
answers: The sea opened instantly
The wind acted for an extended period
The wind blew only in the morning
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the wind acted continuously for a long period.

challenge.question: What detail emphasizes that the crossing took place along an ordered path through the sea?
answers: The waters were a wall on the right and left
Moses stretched out his hand
The wind came from the east
challenge.explanation: The waters on both sides formed a passage between walls through which the Israelites could travel.

questions.question: What can we understand from the description “the waters were a wall”?
answers: The waters stood on both sides of the Israelites
The waters receded on only one side
The waters disappeared completely
questions.explanation: The waters stood like walls beside the path, on the Israelites’ right and left; they did not disappear.

questions.question: What does “all that night” show about the process described?
answers: The sea opened instantly
The wind acted for an extended period
The wind blew only in the morning
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the wind acted continuously for a long period.

questions.question: What detail emphasizes that the crossing took place along an ordered path through the sea?
answers: The waters were a wall on the right and left
Moses stretched out his hand
The wind came from the east
questions.explanation: The waters on both sides formed a passage between walls through which the Israelites could travel.

paragraphs.title: The Egyptians Enter the Sea and Become Afraid

easy.question: Who pursued the Israelites?
answers: The Egyptians
The Philistines
The Amalekites
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the Egyptians pursued them.

easy.question: When did the Lord look upon the Egyptian camp?
answers: In the evening
During the morning watch
At noon
easy.explanation: The passage says that this happened during the morning watch.

easy.question: What did the Egyptians say when they realized that the situation was dangerous?
answers: Let us return to Egypt
Let us cross the sea
Let us flee from Israel
easy.explanation: The Egyptians said, “Let us flee from the face of Israel.”

medium.question: What caused the Egyptians to drive their chariots heavily?
answers: The Lord took off their chariot wheels
The sea closed immediately
The Israelites stopped them
medium.explanation: After the Lord removed the chariot wheels, the Egyptians drove with difficulty.

medium.question: What did the Lord do to the Egyptian camp?
answers: He lit up the camp
He troubled and confused the camp
He rescued the camp
medium.explanation: The Lord caused confusion and difficulty in the Egyptian camp.

medium.question: What happened according to the order of events in these verses?
answers: The Egyptians retreated and then entered the sea
The Lord removed the wheels before the Egyptians pursued
The Egyptians entered the sea, the Lord troubled their camp, and then they wanted to flee
medium.explanation: First the Egyptians entered the sea; then the Lord affected their camp and chariots, and finally they said they wanted to flee.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the Lord looking upon the Egyptian camp through the pillar of fire and cloud?
answers: The Lord used the pillar that guided Israel to act against Egypt
The Egyptians started a fire in their camp
The Israelites were not near the sea
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the pillar of fire and cloud with the action that troubled the Egyptian camp.

challenge.question: Why did the Egyptians say, “The Lord fighteth for them”?
answers: Israel had captured the Egyptian chariots
The Egyptians realized that the Lord was helping Israel and attacking them
Moses fought them with a sword
challenge.explanation: The Egyptians connected the problems with their chariots and camp to the Lord’s action and realized that He was fighting for Israel.

challenge.question: What does “all Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen” emphasize?
answers: Only Pharaoh entered the sea
Only the horsemen pursued Israel
Pharaoh’s entire pursuing military force entered after Israel
challenge.explanation: The phrase lists the horses, chariots, and horsemen, emphasizing that the entire pursuing force followed Israel.

questions.question: What can we infer from the Lord looking upon the Egyptian camp through the pillar of fire and cloud?
answers: The Lord used the pillar that guided Israel to act against Egypt
The Egyptians started a fire in their camp
The Israelites were not near the sea
questions.explanation: The verse connects the pillar of fire and cloud with the action that troubled the Egyptian camp.

questions.question: Why did the Egyptians say, “The Lord fighteth for them”?
answers: Israel had captured the Egyptian chariots
The Egyptians realized that the Lord was helping Israel and attacking them
Moses fought them with a sword
questions.explanation: The Egyptians connected the problems with their chariots and camp to the Lord’s action and realized that He was fighting for Israel.

questions.question: What does “all Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen” emphasize?
answers: Only Pharaoh entered the sea
Only the horsemen pursued Israel
Pharaoh’s entire pursuing military force entered after Israel
questions.explanation: The phrase lists the horses, chariots, and horsemen, emphasizing that the entire pursuing force followed Israel.

paragraphs.title: The Waters Return and Israel Is Saved

easy.question: Who commanded Moses to stretch out his hand over the sea?
answers: The Lord
Pharaoh
The Israelites
easy.explanation: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch out thine hand over the sea.”

easy.question: What happened to the Egyptians when the waters returned?
answers: They crossed on dry ground
The waters covered them
They returned to Egypt
easy.explanation: The waters covered Pharaoh’s chariots, horsemen, and entire army.

easy.question: How did the Israelites cross the sea?
answers: In boats
By swimming
On dry ground, with the waters as a wall on their right and left
easy.explanation: The Israelites walked on dry ground through the sea, with the waters standing on both sides.

medium.question: What was the result of Moses stretching out his hand over the sea?
answers: The waters returned and covered the Egyptians
The sea disappeared completely
The Israelites returned to Egypt
medium.explanation: After Moses stretched out his hand, the waters returned and covered Pharaoh’s army.

medium.question: In “the sea returned to his strength,” what happened to the sea?
answers: It returned to its normal condition
It moved to a new place
It moved toward the Israelites
medium.explanation: The context shows that the sea returned to its normal state after Israel had crossed on dry ground.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: The Egyptians drowned, Moses received the command, and Israel crossed
Israel crossed, the Egyptians returned, and Moses stretched out his hand
The Lord commanded Moses, Moses stretched out his hand, and the waters returned
medium.explanation: First the Lord gave the command; then Moses stretched out his hand, and the sea returned to its place.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “there remained not so much as one of them” emphasize?
answers: Not one of the Egyptians remained
Only one horseman remained
Most of the Egyptians survived
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that not even one of Pharaoh’s army survived.

challenge.question: What is the main contrast between the fate of Israel and the Egyptians at the sea?
answers: Israel crossed at night and the Egyptians by day
Israel crossed on dry ground, while the Egyptians were covered by the waters
Israel traveled in chariots and the Egyptians walked
challenge.explanation: Israel was saved and walked on dry ground, while the Egyptians were overwhelmed by the waters.

challenge.question: Although Moses stretched out his hand, to whom does the verse attribute the salvation?
answers: The army of Israel
Moses alone
The Lord
challenge.explanation: Verse 30 explicitly says, “The Lord saved Israel that day.”

questions.question: What does the phrase “there remained not so much as one of them” emphasize?
answers: Not one of the Egyptians remained
Only one horseman remained
Most of the Egyptians survived
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that not even one of Pharaoh’s army survived.

questions.question: What is the main contrast between the fate of Israel and the Egyptians at the sea?
answers: Israel crossed at night and the Egyptians by day
Israel crossed on dry ground, while the Egyptians were covered by the waters
Israel traveled in chariots and the Egyptians walked
questions.explanation: Israel was saved and walked on dry ground, while the Egyptians were overwhelmed by the waters.

questions.question: Although Moses stretched out his hand, to whom does the verse attribute the salvation?
answers: The army of Israel
Moses alone
The Lord
questions.explanation: Verse 30 explicitly says, “The Lord saved Israel that day.”

paragraphs.title: Israel Sees the Great Power and Believes

easy.question: What did the Israelites see?
answers: The Lord’s great work
The Temple
The land of Canaan
easy.explanation: The Israelites saw the great work that the Lord had done against the Egyptians.

easy.question: Whom did the people fear?
answers: Moses
The Lord
Pharaoh
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the people feared the Lord.

easy.question: In whom did the Israelites believe?
answers: Pharaoh and his army
Egypt and the river
The Lord and His servant Moses
easy.explanation: The verse says that Israel believed in the Lord and in His servant Moses.

medium.question: What caused the Israelites to fear the Lord and believe in Him?
answers: The great work He had done against Egypt
A promise from Pharaoh
Their arrival in Canaan
medium.explanation: The people saw the great work the Lord had done against Egypt, and afterward they feared and believed in Him.

medium.question: In the phrase “the great work which the Lord did,” what does “work” refer to?
answers: A physical body part
A great act of power
A high place
